NDT training in Everett, WA: how it works for aerospace shops and their technicians

Short answer: Everett technicians study NDT theory online at their own pace on the Atlantis portal, ask an ASNT NDT Level III whenever something is unclear, rehearse in the Practical NDT browser simulator, and complete hands-on work at their employer's own shop or hangar. Atlantis NDT has no classroom in Everett. The courses follow ASNT SNT-TC-1A, and the employer, not the course, certifies each technician. We reply within one business day.

Search for "ndt training Everett" and most of what you find is shaped by one fact: this is an aircraft town. Wings, fuselage sections, landing-gear parts, brackets and fittings move through Snohomish County every day, and every one of them has an inspection record behind it. A technician who can perform fluorescent penetrant, eddy current and ultrasonic examinations to a written procedure, and document them cleanly, is employable across a long list of shops between Mukilteo and Arlington.

Aerospace work also sets a high bar for paperwork. Auditors from the primes and from Nadcap read certification files closely, and a gap in training hours or an expired vision test can stop a shop from shipping parts. That is why the training described here puts as much weight on records and procedures as on technique.

Ready to talk about a programme? Request an Everett training quote and list the methods, levels and number of people. Background reading: the NDT training FAQ, the full training catalogue and the national US training guide.

How to get NDT certified in Everett: the SNT-TC-1A path step by step

Certification in Washington follows the national model. SNT-TC-1A is a recommended practice, and each employer writes its own procedure for qualifying people, called a written practice. The order of events looks like this for a Snohomish County technician:

  1. Secure a sponsoring employer. Because the employer signs the certificate, you need one whose written practice covers the method and level you are after. Many Everett trainees start as helpers or production inspectors and move into NDT from inside the company.
  2. Finish the formal training hours set in that written practice. Self-paced theory on the Atlantis portal covers the classroom portion; the training-requirements matrix lists SNT-TC-1A recommended hours, and aerospace customers often expect more.
  3. Build documented experience working under a certified Level II or Level III. Keep the log from your first shift, because experience usually takes longer than study.
  4. Pass the general examination covering the principles, equipment and vocabulary of the method.
  5. Pass the specific examination, written around the shop's own procedures, equipment and acceptance criteria, which in aerospace come from the customer's specification.
  6. Pass the practical examination on representative parts, graded by a Level III or an examiner working under one.
  7. Pass a vision test for near-vision acuity and colour contrast at the interval the written practice sets. Check what applies with the SNT-TC-1A eligibility checker.
  8. Receive the employer's signed certification for that method and level.
  9. Recertify when the written practice says so, which SNT-TC-1A recommends should be no longer than five years.

Prefer a credential that moves with you when you change employers? ASNT central certification (ASNT 9712 for Level I and II, and the ASNT NDT Level III examinations) is the alternative, and Atlantis prepares candidates for it. See ASNT certification.

Level 1, Level 2 and Level 3 NDT courses for Everett technicians

A Level 1 course teaches the fundamentals a technician needs to perform examinations under supervision. A Level 2 course adds set-up, calibration, interpretation and reporting against a procedure. Level III preparation covers the Basic and Method examinations for people who will write procedures and examine others. The table shows how each method connects to Everett-area work.

MethodWhat the course coversWhere it is used around Everett
PTFluorescent and visible penetrant processes, cleaning and etch effects, dwell, developer, ultraviolet viewing conditions, evaluationMachined aluminium and titanium parts, forgings and castings coming out of supplier shops and surface-finishing lines
ETImpedance-plane display, probe and frequency choice, reference standards, surface and bolt-hole techniques, conductivityFastener holes, skins and fittings in aircraft maintenance; crack checks on in-service structure
UTSound physics, straight-beam and angle-beam technique, calibration blocks, composite laminate inspection, reportingComposite and bonded structure, thick machined parts, weld examination in marine and refinery work
MTMagnetising techniques, field direction, wet fluorescent particles, demagnetisation, indication evaluationSteel landing-gear and actuator components, tooling, structural and refinery welds
VTLighting and acuity, measuring tools, discontinuity recognition, borescope use, reportingEvery production and maintenance task; weld visual on structural, marine and pressure work
RTExposure technique, image quality indicators, film and digital interpretation, radiation safety principlesCastings and assemblies where specified; piping and vessel welds at the northern refineries

Most Everett newcomers begin with PT and VT, add MT, and move on to ET or UT once a supervisor is ready to sign off their experience. See the method pages for eddy current training and magnetic particle training.

Ultrasonic testing (UT) training in Everett, and why penetrant and eddy current matter just as much

In a refinery town UT usually means weld examination and wall-thickness readings. Around Paine Field, ultrasonic work is just as likely to mean looking for disbonds, porosity and delamination in carbon-fibre laminate, or checking thick aluminium plate and forgings before machining. The ultrasonic testing training course covers both: the shared physics of velocity, attenuation and beam spread, the use of reference standards, straight-beam technique for laminates and plate, and angle-beam technique for welds. Self-check your theory with the UT Level 2 practice questions.

Penetrant is the single most common method on aerospace production floors, because so many parts are non-magnetic alloys with machined surfaces. Good PT training goes past "apply, wait, wipe, develop": it covers why surface preparation and etching matter on smeared metal, how process control checks keep a line honest, and how to describe an indication so a reviewer can disposition it. Eddy current earns its place in maintenance, where a technician can find a crack around a fastener without removing paint. The ET course teaches impedance-plane reading and calibration on reference standards; it is a training course, and the Level III review for ET programmes is arranged through the employer's own Level III.

Where NDT technicians work around Everett

Airliner assembly. Boeing's Everett factory at Paine Field builds widebody aircraft, including the 767 family, the KC-46 tanker derived from it, and the 777 family. Boeing qualifies its own inspectors through internal programmes, and its job listings for NDT roles in Everett appear regularly. Outside training is most useful as preparation for those roles and for the much larger supplier base around them.

The supplier and finishing base. Snohomish County has dozens of machine shops, composite fabricators, heat-treat and surface-finishing plants and assembly subcontractors working for the primes. Their NDT departments are often small, which means one or two technicians must cover several methods and keep the certification file audit-ready.

Aircraft maintenance. Paine Field hosts heavy maintenance and modification work, including Aviation Technical Services. FAA repair stations perform NDT to the aircraft manufacturer's NDT manual and their own repair station manual, and eddy current and penetrant are daily tools. The aviation NDT training page explains how maintenance work differs from production work.

Navy and marine work. Naval Station Everett homeports Navy surface ships, and the waterfront and the nearby boatyards generate weld, thickness and coating-related inspection. Navy contract work brings its own personnel requirements set by the contract and administered by the employer's Level III.

Refineries to the north. Two refineries at Anacortes and two near Ferndale and Cherry Point run turnarounds that draw technicians from across Puget Sound. That work follows API inspection codes and ASME practice, with UT thickness, RT, MT and VT in heavy use. Atlantis does not train for the API inspector certifications; it trains the NDT technicians who support those inspectors.

Port and construction. The Port of Everett moves aerospace components and other heavy cargo, and bridge, building and utility steel across the county follows AWS D1.1 and D1.5. Welding inspection is a separate discipline, and where it matters Atlantis offers a six-day AWS CWI exam-prep course; AWS runs the examination and issues the certification.

For wage information, see the NDT salary guide, which cites public sources rather than local estimates.

NDT schools and classes near Everett: what to compare

People searching "ndt school near me" from Everett usually come across three kinds of option. Clover Park Technical College in Lakewood runs a college NDT programme with certificates and an associate degree covering visual, magnetic particle, penetrant, radiographic, ultrasonic and eddy current testing. The Washington Aerospace Training and Research Center at Paine Field, run by Edmonds College, lists a short NDI programme among its aerospace courses. And there are self-paced online providers, Atlantis among them, where the theory is studied remotely and the practical happens with an employer.

A full college programme suits someone with time to study before looking for work and a wish for extended lab practice. A short course suits someone who wants a fast route into an aerospace job. Self-paced theory suits technicians already employed on rotating shifts, and companies that want staff examined on their own parts and procedures. None of them, on its own, makes a person certified.

Questions worth putting to any provider:

  • Will the training hours count under the written practice of the employer you are targeting?
  • Who grades the practical examination, and what certification does that person hold?
  • Does the course cover the specifications your target shops work to, or only general theory?
  • Does the provider say plainly that the employer certifies, or does it suggest the course does?
  • How long can you keep using the study material after you finish?

Atlantis NDT has no classroom in Everett and does not claim one. What it offers is online theory with Level III support, simulator rehearsal, and hands-on practical work and examinations at the sponsoring employer's facility. The near-me guide explains how to approach shops about sponsorship.

Online NDT training in Washington

Washington technicians can complete Level I and Level II theory online through the Atlantis portal, and Level III candidates can prepare for the ASNT Basic and Method examinations the same way. Access opens the moment you enrol, courses run year-round, and the Level III answers questions as they come up. For an Everett production worker on second shift or a maintenance technician working nights in a hangar, that flexibility is usually the deciding factor. The hands-on component and practical examination are done in person with the employer. More detail is on the online NDT training page and the Washington training page.

Before enrolling, ask your employer how many classroom hours its written practice accepts from online study. A short email to the shop's Level III can save you from completing hours that do not count.

Training a crew at your Everett facility

An Everett supplier qualifying several technicians at once can keep production running: the crew studies theory online in their own time, and the specific and practical examinations take place at your shop, on your penetrant line, your eddy current instruments and your own reference parts. For aerospace shops this matters, because the specific examination should reflect the acceptance criteria your customers actually impose.

Shops preparing for a prime or Nadcap audit often find the written practice has drifted from how the work is now done. Atlantis builds and revises written practices on SNT-TC-1A and aligns them with the customer flow-down and AC7114, and the shop's Level III confirms the fit against each purchase order. See written practice development, corporate NDT training and outsourced Level III consulting, or ask about training an Everett crew.

Radiography licensing in Washington

Radiography is regulated separately from method certification. Washington is an NRC Agreement State, so the state Department of Health licenses radioactive materials, including industrial radiography sources, and inspects licensees. Any company running radiography in Snohomish County, whether on refinery piping or on castings in a fabrication shop, needs that licence, and its radiographers must meet the training, examination and supervision conditions the licence and state rules set. Cabinet X-ray systems used inside aerospace plants fall under the state's radiation machine rules instead. An RT method course, from Atlantis or anyone else, teaches technique and interpretation; it does not license a radiographer or authorise anyone to handle a source. Confirm current requirements with the Department of Health.

Practise before your practical exam

Between study sessions, the Practical NDT browser simulator lets you rehearse set-ups, scan coverage and interpretation. Everett trainees often use the aviation workplace and the eddy current simulator. The NDT practice tests check general and method theory. Neither replaces hands-on training, logged experience or a practical examination on real parts under the employer's written practice.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, founder of Atlantis NDT and an ASNT NDT Level III in UT, RT, MT, PT and VT, with more than eleven years of international field experience. He writes the course content, oversees examinations and reviews written practices and procedures for employers.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Everett

How do I become an NDT technician in Washington?

Find an employer with an SNT-TC-1A written practice, complete the training hours and supervised experience it requires, pass the general, specific and practical examinations and a vision test, and the employer certifies you. Atlantis supplies the theory, exam preparation and Level III support.

Is there an NDT school near Everett?

College programmes exist in western Washington, including Clover Park Technical College in Lakewood, and short aerospace courses run at Paine Field. Atlantis has no building in Everett; its theory is online and the practical is done at an employer's facility.

Which NDT method should I learn first for aerospace jobs?

Penetrant and visual testing are the usual starting points, followed by magnetic particle. Eddy current and ultrasonic testing come next once you have supervised experience.

Can I take NDT classes online in Washington?

Yes, for theory. The portal covers Level I and II classroom content and Level III preparation. Practical training and the practical examination are hands-on with an employer.

Does Boeing accept outside NDT training?

Boeing qualifies its own inspectors through internal programmes, so check each posting's requirements. Solid method training is useful preparation, and supplier shops across the county certify people under their own written practices.

How long does it take to reach Level 2?

The written practice decides. SNT-TC-1A recommends minimum training and experience hours for each method, and the experience log is usually the slow part. The training-requirements matrix shows the recommended figures.

What does NDT training cost in Everett?

The published US fees for standard courses appear in the table on this page. Group and onsite programmes are quoted after we know the methods, levels and head-count.

Will my certificate transfer if I move to another aerospace shop?

Not automatically. The new employer reviews your training, experience and examination records and certifies you under its own written practice. ASNT central certification is the portable option.

Can I prepare for ASNT Level III from Everett?

Yes. Level III preparation is self-paced online with Level III Q&A. See ASNT Level III training.

Are there training guides for other Puget Sound cities?

Yes: Seattle, Tacoma, Bremerton, Spokane and Portland.
